issues.summary: set_language/set_config_overrides silently have no effect once utils' lazy caches are populated

issues.summary: load_yaml swallows missing/invalid base files and returns {}, while utils getters advertise a RuntimeError that can never fire
issues.suggestion: Pick one error contract: let load_yaml raise for the packaged base file (it is a packaging error, not a runtime condition) and drop the dead None checks, or make the getters validate non-empty results and raise.
evidence: load_yaml: except FileNotFoundError / yaml.YAMLError -> logger.error(...); return {} (verified for a nonexistent file).
utils.get_enum_maps/_get_unit_metadata_dict/get_sensors_yaml: 'if _X is None: raise RuntimeError(... failed to load)' is dead code after _ensure_loaded(), since load_* never returns None.
A packaged-resource failure therefore surfaces later as a KeyError (e.g. get_enum_maps()['cardinal_directions'] in degrees_to_cardinal) instead of a clear load error.
load_enums/load_units annotate precise value types but return load_yaml's dict[str, Any].

add.description: locale_loader is a leaf, utils depends only on it, models are self-contained, and controller sits on top, keeping dependency direction readable in a small package.
Siblings import from the package root, so import order in __init__ is load-bearing.

add.header: Global locale state and lazy caches
add.description: Language and overrides live in module globals consumed by lazily populated caches in utils, creating order-dependent behavior.

add.header: Compact modules aligned to domain roles
add.description: controller, config_publisher, state_publisher, preprocessor, locale_loader and models each have a clear single noun responsibility, so a newcomer can locate change points easily.

add.header: Locale and sensor metadata externalized to YAML
add.description: Sensor/unit/enum definitions and translations live in locales/*.yaml rather than code, localizing most extension changes to data files.

add.header: Config models isolated in models package
add.description: Typed config classes (MQTT, TLS, station, extension) are separated from runtime services.
txBatteryStatus, batteryStatus* fields and shutDown are dictated by WeeWX packet keys/service hooks, so they are intentional rather than naming drift.
All config models share extra='forbid', Field descriptions and module loggers, making them easy to navigate.

add.header: Future callbacks form deliberate error boundary
add.description: Executor future callbacks log with exc_info and return so one failing packet task does not kill the service; consistent and intentional.
Locale loader degrades to empty dicts on base-file failure, trading loud failure for availability.
Constants like ARCHIVE_ONLY_MEASUREMENTS, RAIN_EVENT_GAP_S and SETTLE_COUNTDOWN_START carry unit suffixes and explanatory comments, making their purpose clear at call sites.
Controller uses on_mqtt_* and on_weewx_* consistently for event handlers, giving a predictable vocabulary.

add.header: Generic process_packet verb shared across pipeline stages
add.description: Three classes use the same method name for distinct behaviors, so the name reveals little at call sites.
One MQTT client, YAML parser and pydantic for models; no overlapping libraries, keeping footprint small.
publish_discovery iterates a snapshot and process_packet inserts completed entries only, each with a comment explaining the cross-thread reason; keeps mutation bounded and explicit.
Archive SQL aggregation lives in Controller as one long method plus static helpers, making it the main low-level complexity hotspot.

add.header: Controller as composition root with future callbacks
add.description: Controller wires preprocessor and both publishers onto one executor and uses uniform done-callbacks for error logging, keeping failure handling predictable.
Derived rain/ET/temperature keys are defined in controller SQL, units registry mutation and sensors.yaml.

add.header: Regression tests cite upstream issues and are deterministic
add.description: Tests carry docstrings explaining the bug and link issue numbers; no sleeps or timing dependence, so they are stable.

add.header: Controller is the untested orchestration hub
add.description: Only init_mqtt_client and DB-derived helpers are tested, via __new__ stubs; event handlers and config parsing are uncovered.

add.header: Synchronous, small public API with typed config models
add.description: No mixed sync/async; Pydantic models forbid extra fields so config errors surface at the boundary.
set_language/set_config_overrides and lazy caches in utils make lookups order-dependent, which the public API does not signal.
Credentials and TLS context are validated by pydantic models and applied in one client factory, leaving no sibling paths to diverge.
Long comments in controller.py document concrete bug history and constraints (connect_async ordering, unit-group registration, thread-safe snapshots), not code restatement.

add.header: Cohesive models subpackage for config types
add.description: Pydantic config classes are grouped in models/ with a clean re-export, keeping the root focused on publishing logic.

add.header: Package-root imports used for sibling access
add.description: Modules import siblings via 'from . import X', coupling them to __init__ ordering; direct module imports would be more robust.
YAML and config loading is lazy, so importing the package does no I/O.
Language and overrides live in locale_loader globals feeding lazy caches in utils, creating an ordering contract.
models/ keeps each config concern in its own short file, easy to grasp quickly.
Derived-sensor features were bolted into Controller instead of a dedicated aggregates module.

add.header: Core publishers honor documented return contracts
add.description: ConfigPublisher.process_packet returns bool as documented, publish_discovery snapshots then publishes complete entries only, and get_key_config's deepcopy guarantee is documented and held; these were verified, not assumed.

add.header: Global locale state lacks an invalidation contract
add.description: set_language/set_config_overrides mutate module globals that utils caches once; order-of-call is the only thing that makes the documented behavior true.

add.header: Defensive log-and-continue conflicts with raise contracts
add.description: load_yaml returns {} on error while utils getters document RuntimeError, and Controller.__init__ returns early rather than failing, leaving partial objects.
Worker threads share seen_measurements; code builds entries fully before insertion and iterates list() snapshots, avoiding mutation races.
MQTT init order, int/str key merge and archive filtering carry comments explaining why, making edge-case logic checkable.
